item.title: Busqueda de identidad cultural en dos novelas latinoamericanas: Los Pasos Perdidos de Alejo Carpentier y Quarup de Antonio Callado
item.description: Two Latin American works, Quarup (Callado, 1967) and Los pasos perdidos (Carpentier, 1959) interpret in their protagonists the perennial problem of the modern alienated human in the metropolis. The introduction to this thesis shows how this alienated protagonist is a central preoccupation in Latin American literature since the beginning of modern urbanization and industrialization in the hemisphere. item.title: A Survey of Selected Cedar Rapids, Iowa, Business Firms to Determine Office Job Opportunities for High School Graduates
item.description: The purpose of this study was to determine office job opportunities and working conditions for high school graduates in Cedar Rapids, Iowa. It also considered employer opinion on various aspects of high school education in Cedar Rapids, the effect of automation in the small office, and numbers of office machines. item.title: Specification and Automatic Code Generation of the Data Layer for Data-Intensive Web-Based Applications
item.description: In this thesis I propose a new code generation approach to developing data-intensive web-based applications. I hypothesize that it is possible to build a code generator which will significantly improve development of data-intensive web-based applications by generating at least 50% of the data access code based on a specification of the application's data model. item.title: The Vocational Usage of Shorthand by the 1950 and 1954 High School Graduates of Hardin County, Iowa
item.description: The investigator, as a business education teacher, has frequently been asked by school administrators and others to present evidence as to the proper place of shorthand in the high school curriculum. The present investigation was concerned with securing such evidence.

item.title: Written on the Body by Jeanette Winterson in the Context of Nomadology
item.description: This study provides an interpretation of the novel Written on the Body by Jeanette Winterson in the context of nomadology, a post-modern philosophical project initiated by Gilles Deleuze. My analysis, concentrating on the plot and the narrative strategy of the novel, explores the concept of nomadic subjectivity and demonstrates how it is constructed in the text and how, if at all, it can be challenged. item.title: The Place My Words Are Looking for and Other Stories
item.description: The Place My Words Are Looking For and Other Stories is a collection of short fiction and excerpts from a novel. item.title: Naked-Eye Astronomy: Stars, the Sun, the Moon, Planets, and the Deep Sky
item.description: In this textbook the author brings back some of the ‘old’ astronomy, but viewed through the imaginary lens of huge telescopes and orbiting observatories. He teaches us what we can see in the sky without any instrument at all - with the only pre-requisite of access to a dark sky. We learn about lunar / solar eclipses and how contemporary cultures and ancient ancestors around the world discovered the sky.
